provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — inbound PPSX/PPT attachments with embedded OLE Package objects are detectable via email-gateway attachment inspection and endpoint child-process spawning from POWERPNT.EXE, but require content-level visibility

medium — fake-update lures and drive-by download chains are detectable via proxy/DNS reputation on the actor domain and browser-spawned executable-download telemetry, but the specific one-off site limits generalizable signatures

medium — CVE-2014-4114 exploitation is detectable via patch-state monitoring and anomalous child processes / file writes from POWERPNT.EXE (e.g. INF/OLE package execution), but is dated and requires Office process visibility

medium — execution of user-opened droppers with decoy names/icons is detectable via endpoint process-creation telemetry and mark-of-the-web/downloaded-executable launches, but depends on user action and endpoint coverage
medium — second-stage payload retrieval is detectable via process-spawned outbound connections and new-executable file writes, but the commodity single-server C2 gives limited network signature

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — binaries named putty.exe/dwm.exe running from unexpected paths or with wrong signatures/hashes are detectable via name-vs-path/signature baselining, but require endpoint image-metadata visibility

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — domain registration and hosting acquisition occur off-victim; hunt/intel candidate via WHOIS/passive-DNS monitoring and identity-abuse tracking, not endpoint telemetry
low — capability acquisition is off-victim; the downstream execution of each RAT is where detection lands. Intel/hunt candidate via crypter/PDB-string and commodity-RAT family tracking
low — malware staging on adversary infrastructure is off-victim; hunt/intel candidate via URL/content monitoring of known actor domains

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — the packing itself is designed to defeat static signatures; hunt candidate via crypter-stub/YARA and PDB-string artifacts, with behavioral detection deferred to runtime RAT activity. This is one of the four techniques MITRE attributes to G0043
low — RAT keylogging leaves little discrete host signal; hunt candidate via keyboard-hook/API-callback and RAT-process behavioral telemetry rather than a specific event
low — RAT screen capture is difficult to distinguish from legitimate screen APIs; hunt candidate via RAT-process behavior correlation, not a standalone signal
low — microphone access by a RAT is hard to separate from legitimate audio use; hunt candidate via device-access/RAT-behavior telemetry
low — RAT webcam access closely mimics legitimate camera use; hunt candidate via device-access/RAT-behavior telemetry
low — individual file deletions blend with normal activity; hunt candidate via file-deletion auditing correlated with RAT process lineage
